title: Shibhi Studio: Header-right Vinyl + 13-category HDD arm angle mapping (20°–42°)

requirements.summary: Move VinylPlayer into the header/title row and align it to the right on desktop while keeping responsive stacking on smaller screens.
acceptanceCriteria: On desktop (lg+), the vinyl appears visually at the right side of the header/title area for “shibhi.studio”.
On smaller screens, the layout remains responsive (no overlap/cutoff); the vinyl may stack under/near the header but should not appear far down the page compared to the header area.

file_operations.description: Refactor the title area into a responsive header row that places the VinylPlayer at the right end on lg+ (and stacks near the header on smaller screens). Use the existing VinylPlayer component (optionally its compact mode) and remove the current lower-left placement so it no longer appears far down the left column.

requirements.summary: Clamp HDD arm rotation to 20°–42° and linearly map exactly 13 visible categories (1→42°, 13→20°).
acceptanceCriteria: When hovering/selecting the first category in the 13-category set, the arm rotation is exactly 42°.
When hovering/selecting the 13th category in the 13-category set, the arm rotation is exactly 20°.
For categories 2–12, the arm rotation is linearly spaced between 42° and 20° (inclusive) and is clamped so it never goes below 20° or above 42°.
The category list used for this arm mapping contains exactly 13 categories (no more, no less), and the mapping is based on the visible/active category ordering.

file_operations.description: Update the exported categories list so it contains exactly 13 categories in the same visible order used by the UI, ensuring the HDD arm mapping is based on this exact 13-item list.

Adjust HDDHub arm rotation logic to compute a linear mapping from lane index (0..12) to degrees (42..20), clamp to [20, 42], and ensure the default/rest angle also stays within the 20°–42° range when no category is active.

Keep overlay content consistent with the updated 13-category list (remove or reconcile any overlay entries for categories that are no longer present) to avoid mismatches and ensure the visible/active category ordering is the source of truth.
